topic: How does statistical CSI-based precoding affect margin requirements in LEO link budgets compared to terrestrial systems?
consensus_response: Statistical CSI-based precoding affects margin requirements in LEO link budgets by reducing computational overhead but increasing complexity and susceptibility to interference due to high variability in channel conditions. Atmospheric turbulence causes phase errors in the antenna array, leading to beam squint and reduced effectiveness of statistical CSI-based precoding. To mitigate this effect, advanced signal processing techniques, such as machine learning-based precoding, can be integrated with statistical CSI-based precoding. This approach balances improved efficiency with reduced susceptibility to interference.
reference_context: The use of statistical CSI-based precoding in LEO satellite systems is more practical due to its ability to reduce computational overhead compared to instantaneous CSI (ICSI)-based approaches. Statistical CSI varies much slower than ICSI, making it easier to obtain with sufficiently high accuracy.
